problem: Object goal navigation agents generalize poorly across scenes because of weak visual perception and spatial reasoning; existing visual transformers and contextual embeddings do not capture graph-structured relations between objects and edges well.
motivation: Scene-graph relations between objects and edges reflect a deeper understanding of visual perception, which should improve the agent's policy. The paper argues that focusing on target-related zones would make navigation more efficient.
key_idea: Build a Heterogeneous Zone Graph of target-related zones and spatial information, and process it with a Relation-wise Transformer Network that uses node-to-node self-attention and edge-to-node cross-attention to produce navigation actions.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablations can be cited. The claimed benefit comes from modeling relations between previously observed objects and actions, with attention focused on target-related zones.
method: Heterogeneous Zone Graph (HZG): a graph of target-related zones plus spatial information, meant to support efficient navigation.
Relation-wise Transformer Network (RTN): maps the relationship between previously observed objects and navigation actions.
Node-to-node encoder: self-attention over graph nodes.
Edge-to-node decoder: cross-attention from edges to nodes, extracting rich node and edge features with attention on the target-related zone.
